All pilot tasks · Brief · Human verifiers · Auto verifiers · Trajectory verifiers

Cascadia Founders Summit - Executive portrait set: human verifiers

272 human checks, written as 28 rules. 613 further checks (86 rules) are now answered by code: they stay under their K question, marked Code, with how the code checks them. A row comes back to a person only when the code cannot read or find what the check needs. The checks and their K questions are the same as on the V7 site; only the layout changed. Checks that say the same thing about different deliverables are written once, as a rule, with one row per check.

How to read a rule

  1. Read the rule once. It is the same check for every row in its table.
  2. Each row is one original check on one deliverable. Under each row, Reads as gives the rule filled in for that row: the row's file in place of deliverable, and its values in place of the numbered boxes 1 2.
  3. Compare the deliverable with its Source: the supplied image it is made from (click to open it full size) and what the client's files say about it. Then answer Yes or No for that row, as before. Every row keeps its own check ID.

K1 Q1 is the K question a rule scores. Only if present: the rule applies only when that element appears. Critical: a critical-failure check. Look or Measure is the checking method, explained under each rule.

11 of 11 objective rubric questions are answered for this task: 9 by task-specific human verifiers and 2 by the automatic layer.

R028K2 Q3Code18 checks · 18 deliverables

The ground behind the sitter on deliverable is a tone between Fog Grey #D9DDDE and Warm Paper #F2EEE7.

How the code checks: Finds the cut-out sitter, reads the ground round it and checks each channel lies between the two colours. A row comes back to a person when the code cannot read or find what it needs.

Person's method, if a row comes back: Sample the flat ground beside the left shoulder, beside the right shoulder and above the head. Each sample must be within 5 in every RGB channel of one blend between Fog Grey (217,221,222) and Warm Paper (242,238,231). Use the neutral-range calculator in the measurement guide; all three samples must pass. Do not sample hair or anti-aliased edges.

Reference for every row:
summit_brand_notes.txt

R035K2 Q3CodeOnly if present1 check · 1 deliverable

If a portrait appears on deliverable, the ground behind the sitter is a tone between Fog Grey #D9DDDE and Warm Paper #F2EEE7.

How the code checks: Finds each supplied photo on the file, runs the check on each, and checks no other photograph is present. A row comes back to a person when the code cannot read or find what it needs.

Person's method, if a row comes back: Sample the flat ground beside the left shoulder, beside the right shoulder and above the head. Each sample must be within 5 in every RGB channel of one blend between Fog Grey (217,221,222) and Warm Paper (242,238,231). Use the neutral-range calculator in the measurement guide; all three samples must pass. Do not sample hair or anti-aliased edges.

Reference for every row:
summit_brand_notes.txt

Person's method, if a row comes back: Measure, do not estimate. On a measurement copy, mask the named area; exclude photographs and transparent canvas. Count the selected accent-colour pixels and divide by all pixels in that mask. Include text unless the condition excludes it. Test each PDF page or held video frame separately. Yes only when the unrounded percentage is at or below the stated limit. Use the linked measurement guide for rasterisation and colour matching. Each RGB channel must be within 5 of a selected palette colour.
